title: Ethiopian Fried Sweet Bread (Mandazi)
community: Eastern and coastal Ethiopia — the Swahili fried bread tradition
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Mandazi — triangular fried sweet dough with cardamom and coconut milk, shared with the Swahili East African tradition. Served at coastal and eastern Ethiopian community celebrations — a cross-cultural sweet that demonstrates Ethiopia's Indian Ocean connections.
longDesc: Mandazi is the East African fried sweet bread that arrived in Ethiopia through the Swahili coastal connections of its eastern Muslim communities. Ethiopian mandazi uses coconut milk and cardamom for its distinctive flavour.
steps: Dissolve yeast and 1 tsp sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes.
Combine flour, remaining sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, salt.
Add yeast mixture, coconut milk, and oil. Mix to a soft dough.
Roll to 5mm. Cut into triangles or squares.
Deep fry at 170°C 2—3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain. Dust with icing sugar if desired.
chefTips: Coconut milk is the distinctive flavour.
Do not roll too thin — mandazi should puff significantly.
cookingScience: See ETH166 for fried dough science. Coconut milk's MCTs (medium-chain triglycerides) produce a more tender crumb than vegetable oil — the fat molecules are shorter and coat gluten strands more completely, preventing toughening.
culturalNote: Ethiopian mandazi represents the Indian Ocean food connection — the fried sweet bread tradition that moves along the Swahili coast from Mozambique to Somalia has found its Ethiopian expression in the eastern Muslim communities who have maintained these coastal connections for centuries.
